_meta.title: Cisco CCNA Basics
_meta.description: Starter pool with introductory switching, routing, and Cisco administration questions aligned to common CCNA fundamentals.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a VLAN on a switch?
questions.explanation: VLANs logically segment switch ports into different broadcast domains.

questions.text: What type of switch port is used to carry traffic for multiple VLANs?
questions.explanation: Trunk links transport tagged traffic for multiple VLANs.

questions.text: What VLAN behavior is typical for an access port?

answers.text: It carries traffic for a single VLAN
It acts as a routed port by default

questions.explanation: Access ports connect end devices and normally belong to one VLAN.

questions.text: Which route matches all unknown IPv4 destinations?
questions.explanation: The default route is used when no more specific route exists.

questions.text: What metric does OSPF use to choose a best path?
questions.explanation: OSPF uses cost, often derived from interface bandwidth.

questions.text: What is the role of the root bridge in spanning tree?

answers.text: It is the central reference point for path selection

questions.explanation: STP elects a root bridge and calculates loop-free paths from it.

questions.text: What is EtherChannel used for?

answers.text: Bundle multiple links into one logical connection

questions.explanation: EtherChannel improves redundancy and bandwidth by grouping links.

questions.text: What is a key benefit of DHCP snooping?

answers.text: It helps block unauthorized DHCP servers

questions.explanation: DHCP snooping protects clients from rogue DHCP responses.

questions.text: What does switch port security help limit?

answers.text: The MAC addresses allowed on a port

questions.explanation: Port security restricts which MAC addresses can use a switch port.

questions.text: What is required for inter-VLAN routing?

answers.text: A Layer 3 device such as a router or multilayer switch

questions.explanation: Traffic moving between VLANs must be routed by a Layer 3 device.

questions.text: What can an ACL on a Cisco router do?

answers.text: Permit or deny traffic based on matching conditions

questions.explanation: Access control lists filter traffic using rules like IP, protocol, and port.

questions.text: What is NAT overload also commonly called?
questions.explanation: Port Address Translation lets many private hosts share one public IP.

questions.text: Which neighbor discovery protocol is Cisco proprietary?
questions.explanation: Cisco Discovery Protocol is Cisco-specific, while LLDP is vendor-neutral.

questions.text: Which protocol is the vendor-neutral alternative to CDP?
questions.explanation: Link Layer Discovery Protocol works across different vendors.

questions.text: Which remote management protocol is preferred over Telnet for Cisco devices?
questions.explanation: SSH encrypts management traffic, unlike Telnet.

questions.text: How many usable host addresses are available in a /30 IPv4 subnet?
questions.explanation: A /30 has four total addresses: network, two hosts, and broadcast.

questions.text: How does a switch learn entries for its MAC address table?

answers.text: By recording source MAC addresses seen on incoming frames

questions.explanation: Switches learn source MAC addresses and associate them with interfaces.

questions.text: What is the purpose of NTP in a Cisco network?
questions.explanation: Consistent time is important for logs, certificates, and troubleshooting.

questions.text: What is syslog used for?

answers.text: Send device log messages to a central collector

questions.explanation: Syslog centralizes operational and security messages from network devices.

questions.text: Why is saving the running configuration to startup configuration important?

answers.text: So changes persist after a reboot
So the switch learns MAC addresses faster

questions.explanation: Unsaved running configuration changes are lost when the device restarts.
